MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 12, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:01 p.m., on December 12, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 7, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

For Council Member Kelley’s audio teleconference location, a complete copy of the Agenda was
posted by 5:00 p.m. on December 7, 2017, at 573 Hythe Way, Westfield, Indiana.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley (arrived via teleconference at 5:10 p.m.
  during Closed Session and again at 6:09 p.m. for open session)
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs (arrived at 5:22 p.m.)
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel -- Anticipated Litigation. Significant exposure to
  litigation pursuant to subdivision (b) of Section 54956.9: one case. Initiation of
  litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: one case.

City Council Minutes  1  December 12, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member
Kelley joined the meeting via teleconference at 6:09 p.m.)

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council was updated on pending litigation matters
but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Hurricane Help Campaign for Middle School in Port Aransas, Texas

  Community Services Commissioner and Mission Viejo Activities Committee Member,
  Cathy Allen announced that community groups and City staff raised $10,076 for Brundrett
  Middle School in Port Aransas, Texas.

P2.  State of the City

  Mayor Bucknum presented her State of the City video and outgoing remarks.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

“Santa Claus” and “Mrs. Claus”: reported on the status of progress from the North Pole in regard
to Christmas deliveries in Mission Viejo.

Dawn Gabriele and Linda Edgmon: expressed concern with parking issues in the Auburn Ridge
community and asked if it is possible to establish parking restrictions on their streets.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that she was appalled at the comments made, at the last Council
meeting, by the City’s Vector Control Board Member in reference to babies with microcephaly.

Doug Zielasko, Chamber of Commerce Chief Operating Officer, M.V.: presented a survey recap
from the restaurants that participated in the 2017 Mission Viejo Restaurant Week.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

City Council Minutes  2  December 12, 2017
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  3  December 12, 2017
 OLD BUSINESS

9.  Overview of the California Voting Rights Act and Request for Public Input

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg provided a preview of prior and future public hearings and
  noted that tonight's meeting is to present information and allow the City’s consultant and
  demographic expert to explain the mapping tools that will be posted on the City’s website.

  City Attorney Bill Curley stated that the City is following a legal process within the “safe
  harbor” to address the City Council and community’s analysis of potential voting districts.
  He emphasized that nothing has been decided at this point in time and the City is looking
  for community input regarding potential districts.

  Deborah Diep, Executive Director of the Center for Demographic Research at Cal State
  Fullerton: explained the public participation kit which will be posted to the City’s website
  to allow members of the public to produce maps or districts, or simply provide comments
  for submission to the City. She noted that residents will be able to hand-draw districts on
  a map of Mission Viejo or use a more detailed spreadsheet file to create districts.

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: volunteered to serve on a committee to evaluate district elections in
  Mission Viejo. She said that everyone she has spoken to thinks the idea of districting is a
  bad one and she would like to know, on a weekly basis, how many people are contacting
  the City on this topic.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

10.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

11.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell discussed his attendance at the Holly Jolly Tour which is an outing to
see the Home Lighting Contest winners. He noted that he went back the next night to share the
experience with his son and his son’s fiancé. Council Member Goodell wished residents a Merry
Christmas, happy Hanukah and pleasant holiday season.

City Council Minutes  4  December 12, 2017
 Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley commended Cathy Allen and the Mission Viejo Activities Committee
for their efforts in raising funds for the hurricane victims in Port Aransas, and thanked the public
for helping to make it such a success. She also thanked the Activities Committee for providing
Santa’s Workshop again this year. Council Member Kelley complimented Mayor Bucknum for
her work throughout the year in serving as Mayor.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths said hello to his granddaughter, Julia, who was watching the meeting on
television. He stated that this has been a very successful year for the City Council and staff. He
noted that the Council passed a responsible two-year balanced budget and maintained a $27 million
reserve fund. The City is completing the renovation of the Aquatics Center and is working on
revitalizing the civic core. Council Member Raths thanked law enforcement and fire authority
personnel for all that they do to keep Mission Viejo safe. He also thanked the residents of the City
for their trust and confidence in him as a City Council Member and said he looks forward to
continuing his service in 2018. Council Member Raths thanked City Manager Wilber and Assistant
City Manager Rattay for their dedication in keeping staff working smoothly and effectively and
for their responsiveness to him. He thanked City staff for their professionalism and dedication and
concluded with thanks to his Council colleagues for their commitment in serving the community.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs discussed his visit to the four corners holiday area for the first night of
Hanukah. He said it was interesting to hear what people wanted to talk to him about and the one
that got him the most was a little girl who asked him “what do we have to do to get a water slide
in Mission Viejo?” Mayor Pro Tem Sachs discussed a county tour that he and the Chair of Orange
County Fire Authority (OCFA) took yesterday. They witnessed the aftermath of a structure fire in
Santa Ana where 15 or 16 homeless people were living and where one died. They also drove by a
bus shelter and the courthouse where there were many more homeless people living. Mayor Pro
Tem Sachs noted that homelessness is a bigger issue than many understand and OCFA is called to
assist the homeless many times a day. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs announced that the Orange County
Transportation Authority (OCTA) Board of Directors decided that they are no longer interested in
moving forward with the 241/91 freeway overpass which would have helped to relieve traffic
issues in Orange County. He asked residents to drop a note to OCTA and share their thoughts on
that decision. In conclusion, he thanked staff and his colleague for their help and dedication this
year and he wished everyone a Merry Christmas, happy Hanukah and happy New Year.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum reiterated that South County got the short end of the stick when it comes to
completion of the toll road. She said that the Orange County Transportation Authority’s decision
is very frustrating and she asked residents to help communicate their disappointment along with
the City’s efforts to do so. Mayor Bucknum expressed her thanks to the 90 Orange County Fire
Authority firefighters who are out battling fires and putting themselves in harm’s way. She noted
City Council Minutes  5  December 12, 2017
 that one of the fires was started in a homeless encampment and thousands of structures have been
damaged. She said that communities need to make sure that they balance their caring attitudes with
the safety of the public. Mayor Bucknum shared her pride for what the City does for the holidays
and she expressed her thanks for allowing her to serve as Mayor this year. She wished everyone a
wonderful holiday season and in closing, Mayor Bucknum shared a bloopers reel from her State
of the City video.

CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

12.  Selection of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for 2018

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to appoint Ed
  Sachs to serve as Mayor in 2018.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to appoint Greg
  Raths to serve as Mayor Pro Tem in 2018.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:32 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, January 9, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

____________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 9, 2018

City Council Minutes  6  December 12, 2017
